newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power slips amid warmer weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power slips amid warmer weather.

text.p: Spot power prices during peak demand hours in the western U.S. continued to ease amid warmer temperatures, trade sources said Wednesday.
"We started to come off Tuesday, but real-time prices today are down to the mid $20s (per megawatt hour)," said one trader.
"If this trend continues we should have much lower (daily) prices by the weekend," he added.
Another trader noted the supply tightness which took hold early this week when temperatures slid sharply is now mainly felt during morning and evening peaks only.

Bonneville Power Administration continued to refrain from offering surplus power during those hours, but lowered firm prices for shoulder hours on Thursday to $30.00 for Northwest deliveries and $31.00 for California-Oregon border (COB) sales.
"Temperatures in the Northwest are moderating, so it looks like things will come off quite a bit," said one Portland, Ore., trader.
Firm, peak electricity at COB for Thursday was quoted $35.00-40.00 per MWh, compared with $45.00-46.50 on Wednesday.
Off-peak COB for Thursday was little changed at $11.00-12.00.
Thursday firm, peak power at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) eased to $35.00-$40.00, while off-peak was at $11.50-12.50.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity for Thursday was quoted $32.00-40.00, while off-peak was at $10.00-11.00 per MWh.
Thursday firm, peak prices at Four Corners were quoted at $35.00-40.00, while off-peak was at $10.00-11.00.
Palo Verde for the second quarter was $15.25-15.60, while Q2 COB was quoted $11.20-$11.70.
